summary: Defines a projection box; the decal mesh is built from the geometry inside it.
overview: Position, rotate and scale an empty object to define the box. Local -Y is the projection direction — down onto the surface — local X and Z are the footprint, and the scale sets the box size. The decal is then generated from the receiving geometry inside that box.
useCases: Bullet holes, scorch marks and blood splatter.
Painted markings on curved or uneven ground.
Signage that follows the surface it lands on.

params.tuning: Rejects triangles facing too far from the projection direction, which is what stops a decal smearing down a wall it only grazes.
A small push along each vertex normal to avoid z-fighting. Too much and the decal visibly floats.
Which colliders can receive it. Include the ground and walls; exclude characters unless you want decals on them.

gotchas.title: It generates geometry, it does not render a quad
gotchas.body: The decal is built from the receiving surface's own triangles, which is why it follows curves correctly and why a complex surface produces more vertices.

gotchas.title: It is generated, not live
gotchas.body: Moving the receiving geometry afterwards leaves the decal where it was. Regenerate if the surface moves.
